text.WEB: The terror of a king is like the roaring of a lion. He who provokes him to anger forfeits his own life.

text.KJV: It is an honour for a man to cease from strife: but every fool will be meddling.
text.ASV: It is an honor for a man to keep aloof from strife; But every fool will be quarrelling.
text.WEB: It is an honor for a man to keep aloof from strife; but every fool will be quarreling.

text.KJV: The sluggard will not plow by reason of the cold; therefore shall he beg in harvest, and have nothing.
text.ASV: The sluggard will not plow by reason of the winter; Therefore he shall beg in harvest, and have nothing.
text.WEB: The sluggard will not plow by reason of the winter; therefore he shall beg in harvest, and have nothing.

text.KJV: Counsel in the heart of man is like deep water; but a man of understanding will draw it out.
text.ASV: Counsel in the heart of man is `like' deep water; But a man of understanding will draw it out.
text.WEB: Counsel in the heart of man is like deep water; but a man of understanding will draw it out.

text.KJV: Most men will proclaim every one his own goodness: but a faithful man who can find?
text.ASV: Most men will proclaim every one his own kindness; But a faithful man who can find?
text.WEB: Many men claim to be men of unfailing love, but who can find a faithful man?

text.KJV: The just man walketh in his integrity: his children are blessed after him.
text.ASV: A righteous man that walketh in his integrity, Blessed are his children after him.
text.WEB: A righteous man walks in integrity. Blessed are his children after him.

text.KJV: A king that sitteth in the throne of judgment scattereth away all evil with his eyes.
text.ASV: A king that sitteth on the throne of judgment Scattereth away all evil with his eyes.
text.WEB: A king who sits on the throne of judgment scatters away all evil with his eyes.

text.KJV: Who can say, I have made my heart clean, I am pure from my sin?
text.ASV: Who can say, I have made my heart clean, I am pure from my sin?
text.WEB: Who can say, “I have made my heart pure. I am clean and without sin?”

text.KJV: Divers weights, and divers measures, both of them are alike abomination to the LORD.
text.ASV: Diverse weights, and diverse measures, Both of them alike are an abomination to Jehovah.
text.WEB: Differing weights and differing measures, both of them alike are an abomination to Yahweh.

text.KJV: Even a child is known by his doings, whether his work be pure, and whether it be right.
text.ASV: Even a child maketh himself known by his doings, Whether his work be pure, and whether it be right.
text.WEB: Even a child makes himself known by his doings, whether his work is pure, and whether it is right.

text.KJV: The hearing ear, and the seeing eye, the LORD hath made even both of them.
text.ASV: The hearing ear, and the seeing eye, Jehovah hath made even both of them.
text.WEB: The hearing ear, and the seeing eye, Yahweh has made even both of them.

text.KJV: Love not sleep, lest thou come to poverty; open thine eyes, and thou shalt be satisfied with bread.
text.ASV: Love not sleep, let thou come to poverty; Open thine eyes, `and' thou shalt be satisfied with bread.
text.WEB: Don’t love sleep, lest you come to poverty. Open your eyes, and you shall be satisfied with bread.

text.KJV: It is naught, it is naught, saith the buyer: but when he is gone his way, then he boasteth.
text.ASV: It is bad, it is bad, saith the buyer; But when he is gone his way, then he boasteth.
text.WEB: “It’s no good, it’s no good,” says the buyer; but when he is gone his way, then he boasts.

text.KJV: There is gold, and a multitude of rubies: but the lips of knowledge are a precious jewel.
text.ASV: There is gold, and abundance of rubies; But the lips of knowledge are a precious jewel.
text.WEB: There is gold and abundance of rubies; but the lips of knowledge are a rare jewel.

text.KJV: Take his garment that is surety for a stranger: and take a pledge of him for a strange woman.
text.ASV: Take his garment that is surety for a stranger; And hold him in pledge `that is surety' for foreigners.
text.WEB: Take the garment of one who puts up collateral for a stranger; and hold him in pledge for a wayward woman.

text.KJV: Bread of deceit is sweet to a man; but afterwards his mouth shall be filled with gravel.
text.ASV: Bread of falsehood is sweet to a man; But afterwards his mouth shall be filled with gravel.
text.WEB: Fraudulent food is sweet to a man, but afterwards his mouth is filled with gravel.

text.KJV: Every purpose is established by counsel: and with good advice make war.
text.ASV: Every purpose is established by counsel; And by wise guidance make thou war.
text.WEB: Plans are established by advice; by wise guidance you wage war!

text.KJV: He that goeth about as a talebearer revealeth secrets: therefore meddle not with him that flattereth with his lips.
text.ASV: He that goeth about as a tale-bearer revealeth secrets; Therefore company not with him that openeth wide his lips.
text.WEB: He who goes about as a tale-bearer reveals secrets; therefore don’t keep company with him who opens wide his lips.

text.KJV: Whoso curseth his father or his mother, his lamp shall be put out in obscure darkness.
text.ASV: Whoso curseth his father or his mother, His lamp shall be put out in blackness of darkness.
text.WEB: Whoever curses his father or his mother, his lamp shall be put out in blackness of darkness.

text.KJV: An inheritance may be gotten hastily at the beginning; but the end thereof shall not be blessed.
text.ASV: An inheritance `may be' gotten hastily at the beginning; But the end thereof shall not be blessed.
text.WEB: An inheritance quickly gained at the beginning, won’t be blessed in the end.

text.KJV: Say not thou, I will recompense evil; but wait on the LORD, and he shall save thee.
text.ASV: Say not thou, I will recompense evil: Wait for Jehovah, and he will save thee.
text.WEB: Don’t say, “I will pay back evil.” Wait for Yahweh, and he will save you.

text.KJV: Divers weights are an abomination unto the LORD; and a false balance is not good.
text.ASV: Diverse weights are an abomination to Jehovah; And a false balance is not good.
text.WEB: Yahweh detests differing weights, and dishonest scales are not pleasing.

text.KJV: Man's goings are of the LORD; how can a man then understand his own way?
text.ASV: A man's goings are of Jehovah; How then can man understand his way?
text.WEB: A man’s steps are from Yahweh; how then can man understand his way?

text.KJV: It is a snare to the man who devoureth that which is holy, and after vows to make enquiry.
text.ASV: It is a snare to a man rashly to say, `It is' holy, And after vows to make inquiry.
text.WEB: It is a snare to a man to make a rash dedication, then later to consider his vows.

text.KJV: A wise king scattereth the wicked, and bringeth the wheel over them.
text.ASV: A wise king winnoweth the wicked, And bringeth the `threshing' -wheel over them.
text.WEB: A wise king winnows out the wicked, and drives the threshing wheel over them.

text.KJV: The spirit of man is the candle of the LORD, searching all the inward parts of the belly.
text.ASV: The spirit of man is the lamp of Jehovah, Searching all his innermost parts.
text.WEB: The spirit of man is Yahweh’s lamp, searching all his innermost parts.

text.KJV: Mercy and truth preserve the king: and his throne is upholden by mercy.
text.ASV: Kindness and truth preserve the king; And his throne is upholden by kindness.
text.WEB: Love and faithfulness keep the king safe. His throne is sustained by love.

text.KJV: The glory of young men is their strength: and the beauty of old men is the grey head.
text.ASV: The glory of young men is their strength; And the beauty of old men is the hoary head.
text.WEB: The glory of young men is their strength. The splendor of old men is their gray hair.

text.KJV: The blueness of a wound cleanseth away evil: so do stripes the inward parts of the belly.
text.ASV: Stripes that wound cleanse away evil; And strokes `reach' the innermost parts.
text.WEB: Wounding blows cleanse away evil, and beatings purge the innermost parts.

text.KJV: The king's heart is in the hand of the LORD, as the rivers of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will.
text.ASV: The king's heart is in the hand of Jehovah as the watercourses: He turneth it whithersoever he will.
text.WEB: The king’s heart is in Yahweh’s hand like the watercourses. He turns it wherever he desires.

text.KJV: Every way of a man is right in his own eyes: but the LORD pondereth the hearts.
text.ASV: Every way of a man is right in his own eyes; But Jehovah weigheth the hearts.
text.WEB: Every way of a man is right in his own eyes, but Yahweh weighs the hearts.

text.KJV: To do justice and judgment is more acceptable to the LORD than sacrifice.
text.ASV: To do righteousness and justice Is more acceptable to Jehovah than sacrifice.
text.WEB: To do righteousness and justice is more acceptable to Yahweh than sacrifice.

text.KJV: An high look, and a proud heart, and the plowing of the wicked, is sin.
text.ASV: A high look, and a proud heart, `Even' the lamp of the wicked, is sin.
text.WEB: A high look, and a proud heart, the lamp of the wicked, is sin.

text.KJV: The thoughts of the diligent tend only to plenteousness; but of every one that is hasty only to want.
text.ASV: The thoughts of the diligent `tend' only to plenteousness; But every one that is hasty `hasteth' only to want.
text.WEB: The plans of the diligent surely lead to profit; and everyone who is hasty surely rushes to poverty.

text.KJV: The getting of treasures by a lying tongue is a vanity tossed to and fro of them that seek death.
text.ASV: The getting of treasures by a lying tongue Is a vapor driven to and fro by them that seek death.
text.WEB: Getting treasures by a lying tongue is a fleeting vapor for those who seek death.

text.KJV: The robbery of the wicked shall destroy them; because they refuse to do judgment.
text.ASV: The violence of the wicked shall sweep them away, Because they refuse to do justice.
text.WEB: The violence of the wicked will drive them away, because they refuse to do what is right.

text.KJV: The way of man is froward and strange: but as for the pure, his work is right.
text.ASV: The way of him that is laden with guilt is exceeding crooked; But as for the pure, his work is right.
text.WEB: The way of the guilty is devious, but the conduct of the innocent is upright.

text.KJV: It is better to dwell in a corner of the housetop, than with a brawling woman in a wide house.
text.ASV: It is better to dwell in the corner of the housetop, Than with a contentious woman in a wide house.
text.WEB: It is better to dwell in the corner of the housetop, than to share a house with a contentious woman.

text.KJV: The soul of the wicked desireth evil: his neighbour findeth no favour in his eyes.
text.ASV: The soul of the wicked desireth evil: His neighbor findeth no favor in his eyes.
text.WEB: The soul of the wicked desires evil; his neighbor finds no mercy in his eyes.

text.KJV: When the scorner is punished, the simple is made wise: and when the wise is instructed, he receiveth knowledge.
text.ASV: When the scoffer is punished, the simple is made wise; And when the wise is instructed, he receiveth knowledge.
text.WEB: When the mocker is punished, the simple gains wisdom. When the wise is instructed, he receives knowledge.

text.KJV: The righteous man wisely considereth the house of the wicked: but God overthroweth the wicked for their wickedness.
text.ASV: The righteous man considereth the house of the wicked, `How' the wicked are overthrown to `their' ruin.
text.WEB: The Righteous One considers the house of the wicked, and brings the wicked to ruin.

text.KJV: Whoso stoppeth his ears at the cry of the poor, he also shall cry himself, but shall not be heard.
text.ASV: Whoso stoppeth his ears at the cry of the poor, He also shall cry, but shall not be heard.
text.WEB: Whoever stops his ears at the cry of the poor, he will also cry out, but shall not be heard.

text.KJV: A gift in secret pacifieth anger: and a reward in the bosom strong wrath.
text.ASV: A gift in secret pacifieth anger; And a present in the bosom, strong wrath.
text.WEB: A gift in secret pacifies anger; and a bribe in the cloak, strong wrath.

text.KJV: It is joy to the just to do judgment: but destruction shall be to the workers of iniquity.
text.ASV: It is joy to the righteous to do justice; But it is a destruction to the workers of iniquity.
text.WEB: It is joy to the righteous to do justice; but it is a destruction to the workers of iniquity.

text.KJV: The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding shall remain in the congregation of the dead.
text.ASV: The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding Shall rest in the assembly of the dead.
text.WEB: The man who wanders out of the way of understanding shall rest in the assembly of the departed spirits.

text.KJV: He that loveth pleasure shall be a poor man: he that loveth wine and oil shall not be rich.
text.ASV: He that loveth pleasure shall be a poor man: He that loveth wine and oil shall not be rich.
text.WEB: He who loves pleasure shall be a poor man. He who loves wine and oil shall not be rich.

text.KJV: The wicked shall be a ransom for the righteous, and the transgressor for the upright.
text.ASV: The wicked is a ransom for the righteous; And the treacherous `cometh' in the stead of the upright.
text.WEB: The wicked is a ransom for the righteous; the treacherous for the upright.

text.KJV: It is better to dwell in the wilderness, than with a contentious and an angry woman.
text.ASV: It is better to dwell in a desert land, Than with a contentious and fretful woman.
text.WEB: It is better to dwell in a desert land, than with a contentious and fretful woman.

text.KJV: There is treasure to be desired and oil in the dwelling of the wise; but a foolish man spendeth it up.
text.ASV: There is precious treasure and oil in the dwelling of the wise; But a foolish man swalloweth it up.
text.WEB: There is precious treasure and oil in the dwelling of the wise; but a foolish man swallows it up.

text.KJV: He that followeth after righteousness and mercy findeth life, righteousness, and honour.
text.ASV: He that followeth after righteousness and kindness Findeth life, righteousness, and honor.
text.WEB: He who follows after righteousness and kindness finds life, righteousness, and honor.

text.KJV: A wise man scaleth the city of the mighty, and casteth down the strength of the confidence thereof.
text.ASV: A wise man scaleth the city of the mighty, And bringeth down the strength of the confidence thereof.
text.WEB: A wise man scales the city of the mighty, and brings down the strength of its confidence.

text.KJV: Whoso keepeth his mouth and his tongue keepeth his soul from troubles.
text.ASV: Whoso keepeth his mouth and his tongue Keepeth his soul from troubles.
text.WEB: Whoever guards his mouth and his tongue keeps his soul from troubles.

text.KJV: Proud and haughty scorner is his name, who dealeth in proud wrath.
text.ASV: The proud and haughty man, scoffer is his name; He worketh in the arrogance of pride.
text.WEB: The proud and haughty man, “scoffer” is his name; he works in the arrogance of pride.

text.KJV: The desire of the slothful killeth him; for his hands refuse to labour.
text.ASV: The desire of the sluggard killeth him; For his hands refuse to labor.
text.WEB: The desire of the sluggard kills him, for his hands refuse to labor.

text.KJV: He coveteth greedily all the day long: but the righteous giveth and spareth not.
text.ASV: There is that coveteth greedily all the day long; But the righteous giveth and withholdeth not.
text.WEB: There are those who covet greedily all day long; but the righteous give and don’t withhold.

text.KJV: The sacrifice of the wicked is abomination: how much more, when he bringeth it with a wicked mind?
text.ASV: The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination: How much more, when he bringeth it with a wicked mind!
text.WEB: The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination; how much more, when he brings it with a wicked mind!

text.KJV: A false witness shall perish: but the man that heareth speaketh constantly.
text.ASV: A false witness shall perish; But the man that heareth shall speak so as to endure.
text.WEB: A false witness will perish, and a man who listens speaks to eternity.

text.KJV: A wicked man hardeneth his face: but as for the upright, he directeth his way.
text.ASV: A wicked man hardeneth his face; But as for the upright, he establisheth his ways.
text.WEB: A wicked man hardens his face; but as for the upright, he establishes his ways.

text.KJV: There is no wisdom nor understanding nor counsel against the LORD.
text.ASV: There is no wisdom nor understanding Nor counsel against Jehovah.
text.WEB: There is no wisdom nor understanding nor counsel against Yahweh.

text.KJV: The horse is prepared against the day of battle: but safety is of the LORD.
text.ASV: The horse is prepared against the day of battle; But victory is of Jehovah.
text.WEB: The horse is prepared for the day of battle; but victory is with Yahweh.

text.KJV: A GOOD name is rather to be chosen than great riches, and loving favour rather than silver and gold.
text.ASV: A `good' name is rather to be chosen than great riches, `And' loving favor rather than silver and gold.
text.WEB: A good name is more desirable than great riches, and loving favor is better than silver and gold.

text.KJV: The rich and poor meet together: the LORD is the maker of them all.
text.ASV: The rich and the poor meet together: Jehovah is the maker of them all.
text.WEB: The rich and the poor have this in common: Yahweh is the maker of them all.

text.KJV: A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself: but the simple pass on, and are punished.
text.ASV: A prudent man seeth the evil, and hideth himself; But the simple pass on, and suffer for it.
text.WEB: A prudent man sees danger, and hides himself; but the simple pass on, and suffer for it.

text.KJV: By humility and the fear of the LORD are riches, and honour, and life.
text.ASV: The reward of humility `and' the fear of Jehovah `Is' riches, and honor, and life.
text.WEB: The result of humility and the fear of Yahweh is wealth, honor, and life.

text.KJV: Thorns and snares are in the way of the froward: he that doth keep his soul shall be far from them.
text.ASV: Thorns `and' snares are in the way of the perverse: He that keepeth his soul shall be far from them.
text.WEB: Thorns and snares are in the path of the wicked: whoever guards his soul stays from them.

text.KJV: Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.
text.ASV: Train up a child in the way he should go, And even when he is old he will not depart from it.
text.WEB: Train up a child in the way he should go, and when he is old he will not depart from it.

text.KJV: The rich ruleth over the poor, and the borrower is servant to the lender.
text.ASV: The rich ruleth over the poor; And the borrower is servant to the lender.
text.WEB: The rich rule over the poor. The borrower is servant to the lender.

text.KJV: He that soweth iniquity shall reap vanity: and the rod of his anger shall fail.
text.ASV: He that soweth iniquity shall reap calamity; And the rod of his wrath shall fail.
text.WEB: He who sows wickedness reaps trouble, and the rod of his fury will be destroyed.

text.KJV: He that hath a bountiful eye shall be blessed; for he giveth of his bread to the poor.
text.ASV: He that hath a bountiful eye shall be blessed; For he giveth of his bread to the poor.
text.WEB: He who has a generous eye will be blessed; for he shares his food with the poor.

text.KJV: Cast out the scorner, and contention shall go out; yea, strife and reproach shall cease.
text.ASV: Cast out the scoffer, and contention will go out; Yea, strife and ignominy will cease.
text.WEB: Drive out the mocker, and strife will go out; yes, quarrels and insults will stop.

text.KJV: He that loveth pureness of heart, for the grace of his lips the king shall be his friend.
text.ASV: He that loveth pureness of heart, `For' the grace of his lips the king will be his friend.
text.WEB: He who loves purity of heart and speaks gracefully is the king’s friend.

text.KJV: The eyes of the LORD preserve knowledge, and he overthroweth the words of the transgressor.
text.ASV: The eyes of Jehovah preserve `him that hath' knowledge; But he overthroweth the words of the treacherous man.
text.WEB: Yahweh’s eyes watch over knowledge; but he frustrates the words of the unfaithful.

text.KJV: The slothful man saith, There is a lion without, I shall be slain in the streets.
text.ASV: The sluggard saith, There is a lion without: I shall be slain in the streets.
text.WEB: The sluggard says, “There is a lion outside! I will be killed in the streets!”

text.KJV: The mouth of strange women is a deep pit: he that is abhorred of the LORD shall fall therein.
text.ASV: The mouth of strange women is a deep pit: He that is abhorred of Jehovah shall fall therein.
text.WEB: The mouth of an adulteress is a deep pit. He who is under Yahweh’s wrath will fall into it.

text.KJV: Foolishness is bound in the heart of a child; but the rod of correction shall drive it far from him.
text.ASV: Foolishness is bound up in the heart of a child; `But' the rod of correction shall drive it far from him.
text.WEB: Folly is bound up in the heart of a child: the rod of discipline drives it far from him.

text.KJV: He that oppresseth the poor to increase his riches, and he that giveth to the rich, shall surely come to want.
text.ASV: He that oppresseth the poor to increase his `gain', `And' he that giveth to the rich, `shall come' only to want.
text.WEB: Whoever oppresses the poor for his own increase and whoever gives to the rich, both come to poverty.

text.KJV: Bow down thine ear, and hear the words of the wise, and apply thine heart unto my knowledge.
text.ASV: Incline thine ear, and hear the words of the wise, And apply thy heart unto my knowledge.
text.WEB: Turn your ear, and listen to the words of the wise. Apply your heart to my teaching.

text.KJV: For it is a pleasant thing if thou keep them within thee; they shall withal be fitted in thy lips.
text.ASV: For it is a pleasant thing if thou keep them within thee, If they be established together upon thy lips.
text.WEB: For it is a pleasant thing if you keep them within you, if all of them are ready on your lips.

text.KJV: That thy trust may be in the LORD, I have made known to thee this day, even to thee.
text.ASV: That thy trust may be in Jehovah, I have made `them' known to thee this day, even to thee.
text.WEB: I teach you today, even you, So that your trust may be in Yahweh.

text.KJV: Have not I written to thee excellent things in counsels and knowledge,
text.ASV: Have not I written unto thee excellent things Of counsels and knowledge,
text.WEB: Haven’t I written to you thirty excellent things of counsel and knowledge,

text.KJV: That I might make thee know the certainty of the words of truth; that thou mightest answer the words of truth to them that send unto thee?
text.ASV: To make thee know the certainty of the words of truth, That thou mayest carry back words of truth to them that send thee?
text.WEB: To teach you truth, reliable words, to give sound answers to the ones who sent you?

text.KJV: Rob not the poor, because he is poor: neither oppress the afflicted in the gate:
text.ASV: Rob not the poor, because he is poor; Neither oppress the afflicted in the gate:
text.WEB: Don’t exploit the poor, because he is poor; and don’t crush the needy in court;

text.KJV: For the LORD will plead their cause, and spoil the soul of those that spoiled them.
text.ASV: For Jehovah will plead their cause, And despoil of life those that despoil them.
text.WEB: for Yahweh will plead their case, and plunder the life of those who plunder them.

text.KJV: Make no friendship with an angry man; and with a furious man thou shalt not go:
text.ASV: Make no friendship with a man that is given to anger; And with a wrathful man thou shalt not go:
text.WEB: Don’t befriend a hot-tempered man, and don’t associate with one who harbors anger:

text.KJV: Lest thou learn his ways, and get a snare to thy soul.
text.ASV: Lest thou learn this ways, And get a snare to thy soul.
text.WEB: lest you learn his ways, and ensnare your soul.

text.KJV: Be not thou one of them that strike hands, or of them that are sureties for debts.
text.ASV: Be thou not one of them that strike hands, `Or' of them that are sureties for debts.
text.WEB: Don’t you be one of those who strike hands, of those who are collateral for debts.

text.KJV: If thou hast nothing to pay, why should he take away thy bed from under thee?
text.ASV: If thou hast not wherewith to pay, Why should he take away thy bed from under thee?
text.WEB: If you don’t have means to pay, why should he take away your bed from under you?

text.KJV: Remove not the ancient landmark, which thy fathers have set.
text.ASV: Remove not the ancient landmark, Which thy fathers have set.
text.WEB: Don’t move the ancient boundary stone, which your fathers have set up.

text.KJV: Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings; he shall not stand before mean men.
text.ASV: Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings; He shall not stand before mean men.
text.WEB: Do you see a man skilled in his work? He will serve kings. He won’t serve obscure men.

text.KJV: When thou sittest to eat with a ruler, consider diligently what is before thee:
text.ASV: When thou sittest to eat with a ruler, Consider diligently him that is before thee;
text.WEB: When you sit to eat with a ruler, consider diligently what is before you;

text.KJV: And put a knife to thy throat, if thou be a man given to appetite.
text.ASV: And put a knife to thy throat, If thou be a man given to appetite.
text.WEB: put a knife to your throat, if you are a man given to appetite.

text.KJV: Be not desirous of his dainties: for they are deceitful meat.
text.ASV: Be not desirous of his dainties; Seeing they are deceitful food.
text.WEB: Don’t be desirous of his dainties, since they are deceitful food.

text.KJV: Labour not to be rich: cease from thine own wisdom.
text.ASV: Weary not thyself to be rich; Cease from thine own wisdom.
text.WEB: Don’t weary yourself to be rich. In your wisdom, show restraint.

text.KJV: Wilt thou set thine eyes upon that which is not? for riches certainly make themselves wings; they fly away as an eagle toward heaven.
text.ASV: Wilt thou set thine eyes upon that which is not? For `riches' certainly make themselves wings, Like an eagle that flieth toward heaven.
text.WEB: Why do you set your eyes on that which is not? For it certainly sprouts wings like an eagle and flies in the sky.

text.KJV: Eat thou not the bread of him that hath an evil eye, neither desire thou his dainty meats:
text.ASV: Eat thou not the bread of him that hath an evil eye, Neither desire thou his dainties:
text.WEB: Don’t eat the food of him who has a stingy eye, and don’t crave his delicacies:

text.KJV: For as he thinketh in his heart, so is he: Eat and drink, saith he to thee; but his heart is not with thee.
text.ASV: For as he thinketh within himself, so is he: Eat and drink, saith he to thee; But his heart is not with thee.
text.WEB: for as he thinks about the cost, so he is. “Eat and drink!” he says to you, but his heart is not with you.

text.KJV: The morsel which thou hast eaten shalt thou vomit up, and lose thy sweet words.
text.ASV: The morsel which thou hast eaten shalt thou vomit up, And lose thy sweet words.
text.WEB: The morsel which you have eaten you shall vomit up, and lose your good words.

text.KJV: Speak not in the ears of a fool: for he will despise the wisdom of thy words.
text.ASV: Speak not in the hearing of a fool; For he will despise the wisdom of thy words.
text.WEB: Don’t speak in the ears of a fool, for he will despise the wisdom of your words.

text.KJV: Remove not the old landmark; and enter not into the fields of the fatherless:
text.ASV: Remove not the ancient landmark; And enter not into the fields of the fatherless:
text.WEB: Don’t move the ancient boundary stone. Don’t encroach on the fields of the fatherless:

text.KJV: For their redeemer is mighty; he shall plead their cause with thee.
text.ASV: For their Redeemer is strong; He will plead their cause against thee.
text.WEB: for their Defender is strong. He will plead their case against you.

text.KJV: Apply thine heart unto instruction, and thine ears to the words of knowledge.
text.ASV: Apply thy heart unto instruction, And thine ears to the words of knowledge.
text.WEB: Apply your heart to instruction, and your ears to the words of knowledge.

text.KJV: Withhold not correction from the child: for if thou beatest him with the rod, he shall not die.
text.ASV: Withhold not correction from the child; `For' if thou beat him with the rod, he will not die.
text.WEB: Don’t withhold correction from a child. If you punish him with the rod, he will not die.

text.KJV: Thou shalt beat him with the rod, and shalt deliver his soul from hell.
text.ASV: Thou shalt beat him with the rod, And shalt deliver his soul from Sheol.
text.WEB: Punish him with the rod, and save his soul from Sheol.

text.KJV: My son, if thine heart be wise, my heart shall rejoice, even mine.
text.ASV: My son, if thy heart be wise, My heart will be glad, even mine:
text.WEB: My son, if your heart is wise, then my heart will be glad, even mine:

text.KJV: Yea, my reins shall rejoice, when thy lips speak right things.
text.ASV: Yea, my heart will rejoice, When thy lips speak right things.
text.WEB: yes, my heart will rejoice, when your lips speak what is right.

text.KJV: Let not thine heart envy sinners: but be thou in the fear of the LORD all the day long.
text.ASV: Let not thy heart envy sinners; But `be thou' in the fear of Jehovah all the day long:
text.WEB: Don’t let your heart envy sinners; but rather fear Yahweh all day long.

text.KJV: For surely there is an end; and thine expectation shall not be cut off.
text.ASV: For surely there is a reward; And thy hope shall not be cut off.
text.WEB: Indeed surely there is a future hope, and your hope will not be cut off.

text.KJV: Hear thou, my son, and be wise, and guide thine heart in the way.
text.ASV: Hear thou, my son, and be wise, And guide thy heart in the way.
text.WEB: Listen, my son, and be wise, and keep your heart on the right path!

text.KJV: Be not among winebibbers; among riotous eaters of flesh:
text.ASV: Be not among winebibbers, Among gluttonous eaters of flesh:
text.WEB: Don’t be among ones drinking too much wine, or those who gorge themselves on meat:

text.KJV: For the drunkard and the glutton shall come to poverty: and drowsiness shall clothe a man with rags.
text.ASV: For the drunkard and the glutton shall come to poverty; And drowsiness will clothe `a man' with rags.
text.WEB: for the drunkard and the glutton shall become poor; and drowsiness clothes them in rags.

text.KJV: Hearken unto thy father that begat thee, and despise not thy mother when she is old.
text.ASV: Hearken unto thy father that begat thee, And despise not thy mother when she is old.
text.WEB: Listen to your father who gave you life, and don’t despise your mother when she is old.

text.KJV: Buy the truth, and sell it not; also wisdom, and instruction, and understanding.
text.ASV: Buy the truth, and sell it not; `Yea', wisdom, and instruction, and understanding.
text.WEB: Buy the truth, and don’t sell it. Get wisdom, discipline, and understanding.

text.KJV: The father of the righteous shall greatly rejoice: and he that begetteth a wise child shall have joy of him.
text.ASV: The father of the righteous will greatly rejoice; And he that begetteth a wise child will have joy of him.
text.WEB: The father of the righteous has great joy. Whoever fathers a wise child delights in him.

text.KJV: Thy father and thy mother shall be glad, and she that bare thee shall rejoice.
text.ASV: Let thy father and thy mother be glad, And let her that bare thee rejoice.
text.WEB: Let your father and your mother be glad! Let her who bore you rejoice!

text.KJV: My son, give me thine heart, and let thine eyes observe my ways.
text.ASV: My son, give me thy heart; And let thine eyes delight in my ways.
text.WEB: My son, give me your heart; and let your eyes keep in my ways.

text.KJV: For a whore is a deep ditch; and a strange woman is a narrow pit.
text.ASV: For a harlot is a deep ditch; And a foreign woman is a narrow pit.
text.WEB: For a prostitute is a deep pit; and a wayward wife is a narrow well.

text.KJV: She also lieth in wait as for a prey, and increaseth the transgressors among men.
text.ASV: Yea, she lieth in wait as a robber, And increaseth the treacherous among men.
text.WEB: Yes, she lies in wait like a robber, and increases the unfaithful among men.

text.KJV: Who hath woe? who hath sorrow? who hath contentions? who hath babbling? who hath wounds without cause? who hath redness of eyes?
text.ASV: Who hath woe? who hath sorrow? who hath contentions? Who hath complaining? who hath wounds without cause? Who hath redness of eyes?
text.WEB: Who has woe? Who has sorrow? Who has strife? Who has complaints? Who has needless bruises? Who has bloodshot eyes?

text.KJV: They that tarry long at the wine; they that go to seek mixed wine.
text.ASV: They that tarry long at the wine; They that go to seek out mixed wine.
text.WEB: Those who stay long at the wine; those who go to seek out mixed wine.

text.KJV: Look not thou upon the wine when it is red, when it giveth his colour in the cup, when it moveth itself aright.
text.ASV: Look not thou upon the wine when it is red, When it sparkleth in the cup, When it goeth down smoothly:
text.WEB: Don’t look at the wine when it is red, when it sparkles in the cup, when it goes down smoothly.

text.KJV: At the last it biteth like a serpent, and stingeth like an adder.
text.ASV: At the last it biteth like a serpent, And stingeth like an adder.
text.WEB: In the end, it bites like a snake, and poisons like a viper.

text.KJV: Thine eyes shall behold strange women, and thine heart shall utter perverse things.
text.ASV: Thine eyes shall behold strange things, And thy heart shall utter perverse things.
text.WEB: Your eyes will see strange things, and your mind will imagine confusing things.

text.KJV: Yea, thou shalt be as he that lieth down in the midst of the sea, or as he that lieth upon the top of a mast.
text.ASV: Yea, thou shalt be as he that lieth down in the midst of the sea, Or as he that lieth upon the top of a mast.
text.WEB: Yes, you will be as he who lies down in the middle of the sea, or as he who lies on top of the rigging:

text.KJV: They have stricken me, shalt thou say, and I was not sick; they have beaten me, and I felt it not: when shall I awake? I will seek it yet again.
text.ASV: They have stricken me, `shalt thou say', and I was not hurt; They have beaten me, and I felt it not: When shall I awake? I will seek it yet again.
text.WEB: “They hit me, and I was not hurt! They beat me, and I don’t feel it! When will I wake up? I can do it again. I can find another.”

text.KJV: Be not thou envious against evil men, neither desire to be with them.
text.ASV: Be not thou envious against evil men; Neither desire to be with them:
text.WEB: Don’t be envious of evil men; neither desire to be with them:

text.KJV: For their heart studieth destruction, and their lips talk of mischief.
text.ASV: For their heart studieth oppression, And their lips talk of mischief.
text.WEB: for their hearts plot violence, and their lips talk about mischief.

text.KJV: Through wisdom is an house builded; and by understanding it is established:
text.ASV: Through wisdom is a house builded; And by understanding it is established;
text.WEB: Through wisdom a house is built; by understanding it is established;

text.KJV: And by knowledge shall the chambers be filled with all precious and pleasant riches.
text.ASV: And by knowledge are the chambers filled With all precious and pleasant riches.
text.WEB: by knowledge the rooms are filled with all rare and beautiful treasure.

text.KJV: A wise man is strong; yea, a man of knowledge increaseth strength.
text.ASV: A wise man is strong; Yea, a man of knowledge increaseth might,
text.WEB: A wise man has great power; and a knowledgeable man increases strength;

text.KJV: For by wise counsel thou shalt make thy war: and in multitude of counsellors there is safety.
text.ASV: For by wise guidance thou shalt make thy war; And in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.
text.WEB: for by wise guidance you wage your war; and victory is in many advisors.

text.KJV: Wisdom is too high for a fool: he openeth not his mouth in the gate.
text.ASV: Wisdom is too high for a fool: He openeth not his mouth in the gate.
text.WEB: Wisdom is too high for a fool: he doesn’t open his mouth in the gate.

text.KJV: He that deviseth to do evil shall be called a mischievous person.
text.ASV: He that deviseth to do evil, Men shall call him a mischief-maker.
text.WEB: One who plots to do evil will be called a schemer.

text.KJV: The thought of foolishness is sin: and the scorner is an abomination to men.
text.ASV: The thought of foolishness is sin; And the scoffer is an abomination to men.
text.WEB: The schemes of folly are sin. The mocker is detested by men.

text.KJV: If thou faint in the day of adversity, thy strength is small.
text.ASV: If thou faint in the day of adversity, Thy strength is small.
text.WEB: If you falter in the time of trouble, your strength is small.

text.KJV: If thou forbear to deliver them that are drawn unto death, and those that are ready to be slain;
text.ASV: Deliver them that are carried away unto death, And those that are ready to be slain see that thou hold back.
text.WEB: Rescue those who are being led away to death! Indeed, hold back those who are staggering to the slaughter!

text.KJV: If thou sayest, Behold, we knew it not; doth not he that pondereth the heart consider it? and he that keepeth thy soul, doth not he know it? and shall not he render to every man according to his works?
text.ASV: If thou sayest, Behold, we knew not this; Doth not he that weigheth the hearts consider it? And he that keepeth thy soul, doth not he know it? And shall not he render to every man according to his work?
text.WEB: If you say, “Behold, we didn’t know this”; doesn’t he who weighs the hearts consider it? He who keeps your soul, doesn’t he know it? Shall he not render to every man according to his work?

text.KJV: My son, eat thou honey, because it is good; and the honeycomb, which is sweet to thy taste:
text.ASV: My son, eat thou honey, for it is good; And the droppings of the honeycomb, which are sweet to thy taste:
text.WEB: My son, eat honey, for it is good; the droppings of the honeycomb, which are sweet to your taste:

text.KJV: So shall the knowledge of wisdom be unto thy soul: when thou hast found it, then there shall be a reward, and thy expectation shall not be cut off.
text.ASV: So shalt thou know wisdom to be unto thy soul; If thou hast found it, then shall there be a reward, And thy hope shall not be cut off.
text.WEB: so you shall know wisdom to be to your soul; if you have found it, then there will be a reward, your hope will not be cut off.

text.KJV: Lay not wait, O wicked man, against the dwelling of the righteous; spoil not his resting place:
text.ASV: Lay not wait, O wicked man, against the habitation of the righteous; Destroy not his resting-place:
text.WEB: Don’t lay in wait, wicked man, against the habitation of the righteous. Don’t destroy his resting place:

text.KJV: For a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again: but the wicked shall fall into mischief.
text.ASV: For a righteous man falleth seven times, and riseth up again; But the wicked are overthrown by calamity.
text.WEB: for a righteous man falls seven times, and rises up again; but the wicked are overthrown by calamity.

text.KJV: Rejoice not when thine enemy falleth, and let not thine heart be glad when he stumbleth:
text.ASV: Rejoice not when thine enemy falleth, And let not thy heart be glad when he is overthrown;
text.WEB: Don’t rejoice when your enemy falls. Don’t let your heart be glad when he is overthrown;

text.KJV: Lest the LORD see it, and it displease him, and he turn away his wrath from him.
text.ASV: Lest Jehovah see it, and it displease him, And he turn away his wrath from him.
text.WEB: lest Yahweh see it, and it displease him, and he turn away his wrath from him.

text.KJV: Fret not thyself because of evil men, neither be thou envious at the wicked:
text.ASV: Fret not thyself because of evil-doers; Neither be thou envious at the wicked:
text.WEB: Don’t fret yourself because of evildoers; neither be envious of the wicked:

text.KJV: For there shall be no reward to the evil man; the candle of the wicked shall be put out.
text.ASV: For there shall be no reward to the evil man; The lamp of the wicked shall be put out.
text.WEB: for there will be no reward to the evil man; and the lamp of the wicked shall be snuffed out.

text.KJV: My son, fear thou the LORD and the king: and meddle not with them that are given to change:
text.ASV: My son, fear thou Jehovah and the king; `And' company not with them that are given to change:
text.WEB: My son, fear Yahweh and the king. Don’t join those who are rebellious:

text.KJV: For their calamity shall rise suddenly; and who knoweth the ruin of them both?
text.ASV: For their calamity shall rise suddenly; And the destruction from them both, who knoweth it?
text.WEB: for their calamity will rise suddenly; the destruction from them both—who knows?

text.KJV: These things also belong to the wise. It is not good to have respect of persons in judgment.
text.ASV: These also are `sayings' of the wise. To have respect of persons in judgment is not good.
text.WEB: These also are sayings of the wise. To show partiality in judgment is not good.

text.KJV: He that saith unto the wicked, Thou are righteous; him shall the people curse, nations shall abhor him:
text.ASV: He that saith unto the wicked, Thou art righteous; Peoples shall curse him, nations shall abhor him:
text.WEB: He who says to the wicked, “You are righteous”; peoples will curse him, and nations will abhor him—

text.KJV: But to them that rebuke him shall be delight, and a good blessing shall come upon them.
text.ASV: But to them that rebuke `him' shall be delight, And a good blessing shall come upon them.
text.WEB: but it will go well with those who convict the guilty, and a rich blessing will come on them.

text.KJV: Every man shall kiss his lips that giveth a right answer.
text.ASV: He kisseth the lips Who giveth a right answer.
text.WEB: An honest answer is like a kiss on the lips.

text.KJV: Prepare thy work without, and make it fit for thyself in the field; and afterwards build thine house.
text.ASV: Prepare thy work without, And make it ready for thee in the field; And afterwards build thy house.
text.WEB: Prepare your work outside, and get your fields ready. Afterwards, build your house.

text.KJV: Be not a witness against thy neighbour without cause; and deceive not with thy lips.
text.ASV: Be not a witness against thy neighbor without cause; And deceive not with thy lips.
text.WEB: Don’t be a witness against your neighbor without cause. Don’t deceive with your lips.

text.KJV: Say not, I will do so to him as he hath done to me: I will render to the man according to his work.
text.ASV: Say not, I will do so to him as he hath done to me; I will render to the man according to his work.
text.WEB: Don’t say, “I will do to him as he has done to me; I will render to the man according to his work.”

text.KJV: I went by the field of the slothful, and by the vineyard of the man void of understanding;
text.ASV: I went by the field of the sluggard, And by the vineyard of the man void of understanding;
text.WEB: I went by the field of the sluggard, by the vineyard of the man void of understanding;

text.KJV: And, lo, it was all grown over with thorns, and nettles had covered the face thereof, and the stone wall thereof was broken down.
text.ASV: And, lo, it was all grown over with thorns, The face thereof was covered with nettles, And the stone wall thereof was broken down.
text.WEB: Behold, it was all grown over with thorns. Its surface was covered with nettles, and its stone wall was broken down.

text.KJV: Then I saw, and considered it well: I looked upon it, and received instruction.
text.ASV: Then I beheld, and considered well; I saw, and received instruction:
text.WEB: Then I saw, and considered well. I saw, and received instruction:

text.KJV: Yet a little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to sleep:
text.ASV: `Yet' a little sleep, a little slumber, A little folding of the hands to sleep;
text.WEB: a little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to sleep;

text.KJV: So shall thy poverty come as one that travelleth; and thy want as an armed man.
text.ASV: So shall thy poverty come as a robber, And thy want as an armed man.
text.WEB: so your poverty will come as a robber, and your want as an armed man.

text.KJV: These are also proverbs of Solomon, which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out.
text.ASV: These also are proverbs of Solomon, which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out.
text.WEB: These also are proverbs of Solomon, which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out.

text.KJV: It is the glory of God to conceal a thing: but the honour of kings is to search out a matter.
text.ASV: It is the glory of God to conceal a thing; But the glory of kings is to search out a matter.
text.WEB: It is the glory of God to conceal a thing, but the glory of kings is to search out a matter.

text.KJV: The heaven for height, and the earth for depth, and the heart of kings is unsearchable.
text.ASV: As the heavens for height, and the earth for depth, So the heart of kings is unsearchable.
text.WEB: As the heavens for height, and the earth for depth, so the hearts of kings are unsearchable.

text.KJV: Take away the dross from the silver, and there shall come forth a vessel for the finer.
text.ASV: Take away the dross from the silver, And there cometh forth a vessel for the refiner:
text.WEB: Take away the dross from the silver, and material comes out for the refiner;

text.KJV: Take away the wicked from before the king, and his throne shall be established in righteousness.
text.ASV: Take away the wicked `from' before the king, And his throne shall be established in righteousness.
text.WEB: Take away the wicked from the king’s presence, and his throne will be established in righteousness.

text.KJV: Put not forth thyself in the presence of the king, and stand not in the place of great men:
text.ASV: Put not thyself forward in the presence of the king, And stand not in the place of great men:
text.WEB: Don’t exalt yourself in the presence of the king, or claim a place among great men;

text.KJV: For better it is that it be said unto thee, Come up hither; than that thou shouldest be put lower in the presence of the prince whom thine eyes have seen.
text.ASV: For better is it that it be said unto thee, Come up hither, Than that thou shouldest be put lower in the presence of the prince, Whom thine eyes have seen.
text.WEB: for it is better that it be said to you, “Come up here,” than that you should be put lower in the presence of the prince, whom your eyes have seen.

text.KJV: Go not forth hastily to strive, lest thou know not what to do in the end thereof, when thy neighbour hath put thee to shame.
text.ASV: Go not forth hastily to strive, Lest `thou know not' what to do in the end thereof, When thy neighbor hath put thee to shame.
text.WEB: Don’t be hasty in bringing charges to court. What will you do in the end when your neighbor shames you?

text.KJV: Debate thy cause with thy neighbour himself; and discover not a secret to another:
text.ASV: Debate thy cause with thy neighbor `himself', And disclose not the secret of another;
text.WEB: Debate your case with your neighbor, and don’t betray the confidence of another;

text.KJV: Lest he that heareth it put thee to shame, and thine infamy turn not away.
text.ASV: Lest he that heareth it revile thee, And thine infamy turn not away.
text.WEB: lest one who hears it put you to shame, and your bad reputation never depart.

text.KJV: A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in pictures of silver.
text.ASV: A word fitly spoken Is `like' apples of gold in network of silver.
text.WEB: A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in settings of silver.

text.KJV: As an earring of gold, and an ornament of fine gold, so is a wise reprover upon an obedient ear.
text.ASV: `As' an ear-ring of gold, and an ornament of fine gold, `So is' a wise reprover upon an obedient ear.
text.WEB: As an earring of gold, and an ornament of fine gold, so is a wise reprover to an obedient ear.

text.KJV: As the cold of snow in the time of harvest, so is a faithful messenger to them that send him: for he refresheth the soul of his masters.
text.ASV: As the cold of snow in the time of harvest, `So is' a faithful messenger to them that send him; For he refresheth the soul of his masters.
text.WEB: As the cold of snow in the time of harvest, so is a faithful messenger to those who send him; for he refreshes the soul of his masters.

text.KJV: Whoso boasteth himself of a false gift is like clouds and wind without rain.
text.ASV: `As' clouds and wind without rain, `So is' he that boasteth himself of his gifts falsely.
text.WEB: As clouds and wind without rain, so is he who boasts of gifts deceptively.

text.KJV: By long forbearing is a prince persuaded, and a soft tongue breaketh the bone.
text.ASV: By long forbearing is a ruler persuaded, And a soft tongue breaketh the bone.
text.WEB: By patience a ruler is persuaded. A soft tongue breaks the bone.

text.KJV: Hast thou found honey? eat so much as is sufficient for thee, lest thou be filled therewith, and vomit it.
text.ASV: Hast thou found honey? eat so much as is sufficient for thee, Lest thou be filled therewith, and vomit it.
text.WEB: Have you found honey? Eat as much as is sufficient for you, lest you eat too much, and vomit it.

text.KJV: Withdraw thy foot from thy neighbour's house; lest he be weary of thee, and so hate thee.
text.ASV: Let thy foot be seldom in thy neighbor's house, Lest he be weary of thee, and hate thee.
text.WEB: Let your foot be seldom in your neighbor’s house, lest he be weary of you, and hate you.

text.KJV: A man that beareth false witness against his neighbour is a maul, and a sword, and a sharp arrow.
text.ASV: A man that beareth false witness against his neighbor Is a maul, and a sword, and a sharp arrow.
text.WEB: A man who gives false testimony against his neighbor is like a club, a sword, or a sharp arrow.

text.KJV: Confidence in an unfaithful man in time of trouble is like a broken tooth, and a foot out of joint.
text.ASV: Confidence in an unfaithful man in time of trouble Is `like' a broken tooth, and a foot out of joint.
text.WEB: Confidence in someone unfaithful in time of trouble is like a bad tooth, or a lame foot.

text.KJV: As he that taketh away a garment in cold weather, and as vinegar upon nitre, so is he that singeth songs to an heavy heart.
text.ASV: `As' one that taketh off a garment in cold weather, `and as' vinegar upon soda, So is he that singeth songs to a heavy heart.
text.WEB: As one who takes away a garment in cold weather, or vinegar on soda, so is one who sings songs to a heavy heart.

text.KJV: If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he be thirsty, give him water to drink:
text.ASV: If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; And if he be thirsty, give him water to drink:
text.WEB: If your enemy is hungry, give him food to eat. If he is thirsty, give him water to drink:

text.KJV: For thou shalt heap coals of fire upon his head, and the LORD shall reward thee.
text.ASV: For thou wilt heap coals of fire upon his head, And Jehovah will reward thee.
text.WEB: for you will heap coals of fire on his head, and Yahweh will reward you.

text.KJV: The north wind driveth away rain: so doth an angry countenance a backbiting tongue.
text.ASV: The north wind bringeth forth rain: So doth a backbiting tongue an angry countenance.
text.WEB: The north wind produces rain; so a backbiting tongue brings an angry face.

text.KJV: It is better to dwell in the corner of the housetop, than with a brawling woman and in a wide house.
text.ASV: It is better to dwell in the corner of the housetop, Than with a contentious woman in a wide house.
text.WEB: It is better to dwell in the corner of the housetop, than to share a house with a contentious woman.

text.KJV: As cold waters to a thirsty soul, so is good news from a far country.
text.ASV: `As' cold waters to a thirsty soul, So is good news from a far country.
text.WEB: Like cold water to a thirsty soul, so is good news from a far country.

text.KJV: A righteous man falling down before the wicked is as a troubled fountain, and a corrupt spring.
text.ASV: `As' a troubled fountain, and a corrupted spring, `So is' a righteous man that giveth way before the wicked.
text.WEB: Like a muddied spring, and a polluted well, so is a righteous man who gives way before the wicked.

text.KJV: It is not good to eat much honey: so for men to search their own glory is not glory.
text.ASV: It is not good to eat much honey: So `for men' to search out their own glory is grievous.
text.WEB: It is not good to eat much honey; nor is it honorable to seek one’s own honor.

text.KJV: He that hath no rule over his own spirit is like a city that is broken down, and without walls.
text.ASV: He whose spirit is without restraint Is `like' a city that is broken down and without walls.
text.WEB: Like a city that is broken down and without walls is a man whose spirit is without restraint.

text.KJV: As snow in summer, and as rain in harvest, so honour is not seemly for a fool.
text.ASV: As snow in summer, and as rain in harvest, So honor is not seemly for a fool.
text.WEB: Like snow in summer, and as rain in harvest, so honor is not fitting for a fool.

text.KJV: As the bird by wandering, as the swallow by flying, so the curse causeless shall not come.
text.ASV: As the sparrow in her wandering, as the swallow in her flying, So the curse that is causeless alighteth not.
text.WEB: Like a fluttering sparrow, like a darting swallow, so the undeserved curse doesn’t come to rest.

text.KJV: A whip for the horse, a bridle for the ass, and a rod for the fool's back.
text.ASV: A whip for the horse, a bridle for the ass, And a rod for the back of fools.
text.WEB: A whip is for the horse, a bridle for the donkey, and a rod for the back of fools!

text.KJV: Answer not a fool according to his folly, lest thou also be like unto him.
text.ASV: Answer not a fool according to his folly, Lest thou also be like unto him.
text.WEB: Don’t answer a fool according to his folly, lest you also be like him.

text.KJV: Answer a fool according to his folly, lest he be wise in his own conceit.
text.ASV: Answer a fool according to his folly, Lest he be wise in his own conceit.
text.WEB: Answer a fool according to his folly, lest he be wise in his own eyes.

text.KJV: He that sendeth a message by the hand of a fool cutteth off the feet, and drinketh damage.
text.ASV: He that sendeth a message by the hand of a fool Cutteth off `his own' feet, `and' drinketh in damage.
text.WEB: One who sends a message by the hand of a fool is cutting off feet and drinking violence.

text.KJV: The legs of the lame are not equal: so is a parable in the mouth of fools.
text.ASV: The legs of the lame hang loose: So is a parable in the mouth of fools.
text.WEB: Like the legs of the lame that hang loose, so is a parable in the mouth of fools.

text.KJV: As he that bindeth a stone in a sling, so is he that giveth honour to a fool.
text.ASV: As one that bindeth a stone in a sling, So is he that giveth honor to a fool.
text.WEB: As one who binds a stone in a sling, so is he who gives honor to a fool.

text.KJV: As a thorn goeth up into the hand of a drunkard, so is a parable in the mouths of fools.
text.ASV: `As' a thorn that goeth up into the hand of a drunkard, So is a parable in the mouth of fools.
text.WEB: Like a thorn bush that goes into the hand of a drunkard, so is a parable in the mouth of fools.

text.KJV: The great God that formed all things both rewardeth the fool, and rewardeth transgressors.
text.ASV: `As' an archer that woundeth all, So is he that hireth a fool and he that hireth them that pass by.
text.WEB: As an archer who wounds all, so is he who hires a fool or he who hires those who pass by.

text.KJV: As a dog returneth to his vomit, so a fool returneth to his folly.
text.ASV: As a dog that returneth to his vomit, `So is' a fool that repeateth his folly.
text.WEB: As a dog that returns to his vomit, so is a fool who repeats his folly.

text.KJV: Seest thou a man wise in his own conceit? there is more hope of a fool than of him.
text.ASV: Seest thou a man wise in his own conceit? There is more hope of a fool than of him.
text.WEB: Do you see a man wise in his own eyes? There is more hope for a fool than for him.

text.KJV: The slothful man saith, There is a lion in the way; a lion is in the streets.
text.ASV: The sluggard saith, There is a lion in the way; A lion is in the streets.
text.WEB: The sluggard says, “There is a lion in the road! A fierce lion roams the streets!”

text.KJV: As the door turneth upon his hinges, so doth the slothful upon his bed.
text.ASV: `As' the door turneth upon its hinges, So doth the sluggard upon his bed.
text.WEB: As the door turns on its hinges, so does the sluggard on his bed.

text.KJV: The slothful hideth his hand in his bosom; it grieveth him to bring it again to his mouth.
text.ASV: The sluggard burieth his hand in the dish; It wearieth him to bring it again to his mouth.
text.WEB: The sluggard buries his hand in the dish. He is too lazy to bring it back to his mouth.

text.KJV: The sluggard is wiser in his own conceit than seven men that can render a reason.
text.ASV: The sluggard is wiser in his own conceit Than seven men that can render a reason.
text.WEB: The sluggard is wiser in his own eyes than seven men who answer with discretion.

text.KJV: He that passeth by, and meddleth with strife belonging not to him, is like one that taketh a dog by the ears.
text.ASV: He that passeth by, `and' vexeth himself with strife belonging not to him, Is `like' one that taketh a dog by the ears.
text.WEB: Like one who grabs a dog’s ears is one who passes by and meddles in a quarrel not his own.

text.KJV: As a mad man who casteth firebrands, arrows, and death,
text.ASV: As a madman who casteth firebrands, Arrows, and death,
text.WEB: Like a madman who shoots torches, arrows, and death,

text.KJV: So is the man that deceiveth his neighbour, and saith, Am not I in sport?
text.ASV: So is the man that deceiveth his neighbor, And saith, Am not I in sport?
text.WEB: is the man who deceives his neighbor and says, “Am I not joking?”

text.KJV: Where no wood is, there the fire goeth out: so where there is no talebearer, the strife ceaseth.
text.ASV: For lack of wood the fire goeth out; And where there is no whisperer, contention ceaseth.
text.WEB: For lack of wood a fire goes out. Without gossip, a quarrel dies down.

text.KJV: As coals are to burning coals, and wood to fire; so is a contentious man to kindle strife.
text.ASV: `As' coals are to hot embers, and wood to fire, So is a contentious man to inflame strife.
text.WEB: As coals are to hot embers, and wood to fire, so is a contentious man to kindling strife.

text.KJV: The words of a talebearer are as wounds, and they go down into the innermost parts of the belly.
text.ASV: The words of a whisperer are as dainty morsels, And they go down into the innermost parts.
text.WEB: The words of a whisperer are as dainty morsels, they go down into the innermost parts.

text.KJV: Burning lips and a wicked heart are like a potsherd covered with silver dross.
text.ASV: Fervent lips and a wicked heart Are `like' an earthen vessel overlaid with silver dross.
text.WEB: Like silver dross on an earthen vessel are the lips of a fervent one with an evil heart.

text.KJV: He that hateth dissembleth with his lips, and layeth up deceit within him;
text.ASV: He that hateth dissembleth with his lips; But he layeth up deceit within him:
text.WEB: A malicious man disguises himself with his lips, but he harbors evil in his heart.

text.KJV: When he speaketh fair, believe him not: for there are seven abominations in his heart.
text.ASV: When he speaketh fair, believe him not; For there are seven abominations in his heart:
text.WEB: When his speech is charming, don’t believe him; for there are seven abominations in his heart.

text.KJV: Whose hatred is covered by deceit, his wickedness shall be shewed before the whole congregation.
text.ASV: Though `his' hatred cover itself with guile, His wickedness shall be openly showed before the assembly.
text.WEB: His malice may be concealed by deception, but his wickedness will be exposed in the assembly.

text.KJV: Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein: and he that rolleth a stone, it will return upon him.
text.ASV: Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein; And he that rolleth a stone, it shall return upon him.
text.WEB: Whoever digs a pit shall fall into it. Whoever rolls a stone, it will come back on him.

text.KJV: A lying tongue hateth those that are afflicted by it; and a flattering mouth worketh ruin.
text.ASV: A lying tongue hateth those whom it hath wounded; And a flattering mouth worketh ruin.
text.WEB: A lying tongue hates those it hurts; and a flattering mouth works ruin.

text.KJV: Boast not thyself of to morrow; for thou knowest not what a day may bring forth.
text.ASV: Boast not thyself of tomorrow; For thou knowest not what a day may bring forth.
text.WEB: Don’t boast about tomorrow; for you don’t know what a day may bring.

text.KJV: Let another man praise thee, and not thine own mouth; a stranger, and not thine own lips.
text.ASV: Let another man praise thee, and not thine own mouth; A stranger, and not thine own lips.
text.WEB: Let another man praise you, and not your own mouth; a stranger, and not your own lips.

text.KJV: A stone is heavy, and the sand weighty; but a fool's wrath is heavier than them both.
text.ASV: A stone is heavy, and the sand weighty; But a fool's vexation is heavier than they both.
text.WEB: A stone is heavy, and sand is a burden; but a fool’s provocation is heavier than both.

text.KJV: Wrath is cruel, and anger is outrageous; but who is able to stand before envy?
text.ASV: Wrath is cruel, and anger is overwhelming; But who is able to stand before jealousy?
text.WEB: Wrath is cruel, and anger is overwhelming; but who is able to stand before jealousy?

text.KJV: Open rebuke is better than secret love.
text.ASV: Better is open rebuke Than love that is hidden.
text.WEB: Better is open rebuke than hidden love.

text.KJV: Faithful are the wounds of a friend; but the kisses of an enemy are deceitful.
text.ASV: Faithful are the wounds of a friend; But the kisses of an enemy are profuse.
text.WEB: Faithful are the wounds of a friend; although the kisses of an enemy are profuse.

text.KJV: The full soul loatheth an honeycomb; but to the hungry soul every bitter thing is sweet.
text.ASV: The full soul loatheth a honeycomb; But to the hungry soul every bitter thing is sweet.
text.WEB: A full soul loathes a honeycomb; but to a hungry soul, every bitter thing is sweet.

text.KJV: As a bird that wandereth from her nest, so is a man that wandereth from his place.
text.ASV: As a bird that wandereth from her nest, So is a man that wandereth from his place.
text.WEB: As a bird that wanders from her nest, so is a man who wanders from his home.

text.KJV: Ointment and perfume rejoice the heart: so doth the sweetness of a man's friend by hearty counsel.
text.ASV: Oil and perfume rejoice the heart; So doth the sweetness of a man's friend `that cometh' of hearty counsel.
text.WEB: Perfume and incense bring joy to the heart; so does earnest counsel from a man’s friend.

text.KJV: Thine own friend, and thy father's friend, forsake not; neither go into thy brother's house in the day of thy calamity: for better is a neighbour that is near than a brother far off.
text.ASV: Thine own friend, and thy father's friend, forsake not; And go not to thy brother's house in the day of thy calamity: Better is a neighbor that is near than a brother far off.
text.WEB: Don’t forsake your friend and your father’s friend. Don’t go to your brother’s house in the day of your disaster: better is a neighbor who is near than a distant brother.

text.KJV: My son, be wise, and make my heart glad, that I may answer him that reproacheth me.
text.ASV: My son, be wise, and make my heart glad, That I may answer him that reproacheth me.
text.WEB: Be wise, my son, and bring joy to my heart, then I can answer my tormentor.

text.KJV: A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself; but the simple pass on, and are punished.
text.ASV: A prudent man seeth the evil, `and' hideth himself; `But' the simple pass on, `and' suffer for it.
text.WEB: A prudent man sees danger and takes refuge; but the simple pass on, and suffer for it.

text.KJV: Take his garment that is surety for a stranger, and take a pledge of him for a strange woman.
text.ASV: Take his garment that is surety for a stranger; And hold him in pledge `that is surety' for a foreign woman.
text.WEB: Take his garment when he puts up collateral for a stranger. Hold it for a wayward woman!

text.KJV: He that blesseth his friend with a loud voice, rising early in the morning, it shall be counted a curse to him.
text.ASV: He that blesseth his friend with a loud voice, rising early in the morning, It shall be counted a curse to him.
text.WEB: He who blesses his neighbor with a loud voice early in the morning, it will be taken as a curse by him.

text.KJV: A continual dropping in a very rainy day and a contentious woman are alike.
text.ASV: A continual dropping in a very rainy day And a contentious woman are alike:
text.WEB: A continual dropping on a rainy day and a contentious wife are alike:

text.KJV: Whosoever hideth her hideth the wind, and the ointment of his right hand, which bewrayeth itself.
text.ASV: He that would restrain her restraineth the wind; And his right hand encountereth oil.
text.WEB: restraining her is like restraining the wind, or like grasping oil in his right hand.

text.KJV: Iron sharpeneth iron; so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend.
text.ASV: Iron sharpeneth iron; So a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend.
text.WEB: Iron sharpens iron; so a man sharpens his friend’s countenance.

text.KJV: Whoso keepeth the fig tree shall eat the fruit thereof: so he that waiteth on his master shall be honoured.
text.ASV: Whoso keepeth the fig-tree shall eat the fruit thereof; And he that regardeth his master shall be honored.
text.WEB: Whoever tends the fig tree shall eat its fruit. He who looks after his master shall be honored.

text.KJV: As in water face answereth to face, so the heart of man to man.
text.ASV: As in water face `answereth' to face, So the heart of man to man.
text.WEB: Like water reflects a face, so a man’s heart reflects the man.

text.KJV: Hell and destruction are never full; so the eyes of man are never satisfied.
text.ASV: Sheol and Abaddon are never satisfied; And the eyes of man are never satisfied.
text.WEB: Sheol and Abaddon are never satisfied; and a man’s eyes are never satisfied.

text.KJV: As the fining pot for silver, and the furnace for gold; so is a man to his praise.
text.ASV: The refining pot is for silver, and the furnace for gold; And a man is `tried' by his praise.
text.WEB: The crucible is for silver, and the furnace for gold; but man is refined by his praise.

text.KJV: Though thou shouldest bray a fool in a mortar among wheat with a pestle, yet will not his foolishness depart from him.
text.ASV: Though thou shouldest bray a fool in a mortar with a pestle along with bruised grain, Yet will not his foolishness depart from him.
text.WEB: Though you grind a fool in a mortar with a pestle along with grain, yet his foolishness will not be removed from him.

text.KJV: Be thou diligent to know the state of thy flocks, and look well to thy herds.
text.ASV: Be thou diligent to know the state of thy flocks, `And' look well to thy herds:
text.WEB: Know well the state of your flocks, and pay attention to your herds:

text.KJV: For riches are not for ever: and doth the crown endure to every generation?
text.ASV: For riches are not for ever: And doth the crown endure unto all generations?
text.WEB: for riches are not forever, nor does the crown endure to all generations.

text.KJV: The hay appeareth, and the tender grass sheweth itself, and herbs of the mountains are gathered.
text.ASV: The hay is carried, and the tender grass showeth itself, And the herbs of the mountains are gathered in.
text.WEB: The hay is removed, and the new growth appears, the grasses of the hills are gathered in.

text.KJV: The lambs are for thy clothing, and the goats are the price of the field.
text.ASV: The lambs are for thy clothing, And the goats are the price of the field;
text.WEB: The lambs are for your clothing, and the goats are the price of a field.

text.KJV: And thou shalt have goats' milk enough for thy food, for the food of thy household, and for the maintenance for thy maidens.
text.ASV: And `there will be' goats' milk enough for thy food, for the food of thy household, And maintenance for thy maidens.
text.WEB: There will be plenty of goats’ milk for your food, for your family’s food, and for the nourishment of your servant girls.

text.KJV: The wicked flee when no man pursueth: but the righteous are bold as a lion.
text.ASV: The wicked flee when no man pursueth; But the righteous are bold as a lion.
text.WEB: The wicked flee when no one pursues; but the righteous are as bold as a lion.

text.KJV: For the transgression of a land many are the princes thereof: but by a man of understanding and knowledge the state thereof shall be prolonged.
text.ASV: For the transgression of a land many are the princes thereof; But by men of understanding `and' knowledge the state `thereof' shall be prolonged.
text.WEB: In rebellion, a land has many rulers, but order is maintained by a man of understanding and knowledge.

text.KJV: A poor man that oppresseth the poor is like a sweeping rain which leaveth no food.
text.ASV: A needy man that oppresseth the poor Is `like' a sweeping rain which leaveth no food.
text.WEB: A needy man who oppresses the poor is like a driving rain which leaves no crops.

text.KJV: They that forsake the law praise the wicked: but such as keep the law contend with them.
text.ASV: They that forsake the law praise the wicked; But such as keep the law contend with them.
text.WEB: Those who forsake the law praise the wicked; but those who keep the law contend with them.

text.KJV: Evil men understand not judgment: but they that seek the LORD understand all things.
text.ASV: Evil men understand not justice; But they that seek Jehovah understand all things.
text.WEB: Evil men don’t understand justice; but those who seek Yahweh understand it fully.

text.KJV: Better is the poor that walketh in his uprightness, than he that is perverse in his ways, though he be rich.
text.ASV: Better is the poor that walketh in his integrity, Than he that is perverse in `his' ways, though he be rich.
text.WEB: Better is the poor who walks in his integrity, than he who is perverse in his ways, and he is rich.

text.KJV: Whoso keepeth the law is a wise son: but he that is a companion of riotous men shameth his father.
text.ASV: Whoso keepeth the law is a wise son; But he that is a companion of gluttons shameth his father.
text.WEB: Whoever keeps the law is a wise son; but he who is a companion of gluttons shames his father.

text.KJV: He that by usury and unjust gain increaseth his substance, he shall gather it for him that will pity the poor.
text.ASV: He that augmenteth his substance by interest and increase, Gathereth it for him that hath pity on the poor.
text.WEB: He who increases his wealth by excessive interest gathers it for one who has pity on the poor.

text.KJV: He that turneth away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer shall be abomination.
text.ASV: He that turneth away his ear from hearing the law, Even his prayer is an abomination.
text.WEB: He who turns away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer is an abomination.

text.KJV: Whoso causeth the righteous to go astray in an evil way, he shall fall himself into his own pit: but the upright shall have good things in possession.
text.ASV: Whoso causeth the upright to go astray in an evil way, He shall fall himself into his own pit; But the perfect shall inherit good.
text.WEB: Whoever causes the upright to go astray in an evil way, he will fall into his own trap; but the blameless will inherit good.

text.KJV: The rich man is wise in his own conceit; but the poor that hath understanding searcheth him out.
text.ASV: The rich man is wise in his own conceit; But the poor that hath understanding searcheth him out.
text.WEB: The rich man is wise in his own eyes; but the poor who has understanding sees through him.

text.KJV: When righteous men do rejoice, there is great glory: but when the wicked rise, a man is hidden.
text.ASV: When the righteous triumph, there is great glory; But when the wicked rise, men hide themselves.
text.WEB: When the righteous triumph, there is great glory; but when the wicked rise, men hide themselves.

text.KJV: He that covereth his sins shall not prosper: but whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall have mercy.
text.ASV: He that covereth his transgressions shall not prosper: But whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall obtain mercy.
text.WEB: He who conceals his sins doesn’t prosper, but whoever confesses and renounces them finds mercy.

text.KJV: Happy is the man that feareth alway: but he that hardeneth his heart shall fall into mischief.
text.ASV: Happy is the man that feareth alway; But he that hardeneth his heart shall fall into mischief.
text.WEB: Blessed is the man who always fears; but one who hardens his heart falls into trouble.

text.KJV: As a roaring lion, and a ranging bear; so is a wicked ruler over the poor people.
text.ASV: `As' a roaring lion, and a ranging bear, `So is' a wicked ruler over a poor people.
text.WEB: As a roaring lion or a charging bear, so is a wicked ruler over helpless people.

text.KJV: The prince that wanteth understanding is also a great oppressor: but he that hateth covetousness shall prolong his days.
text.ASV: The prince that lacketh understanding is also a great oppressor; `But' he that hateth covetousness shall prolong his days.
text.WEB: A tyrannical ruler lacks judgment. One who hates ill-gotten gain will have long days.

text.KJV: A man that doeth violence to the blood of any person shall flee to the pit; let no man stay him.
text.ASV: A man that is laden with the blood of any person Shall flee unto the pit; let no man stay him.
text.WEB: A man who is tormented by life blood will be a fugitive until death; no one will support him.

text.KJV: Whoso walketh uprightly shall be saved: but he that is perverse in his ways shall fall at once.
text.ASV: Whoso walketh uprightly shall be delivered; But he that is perverse in `his' ways shall fall at once.
text.WEB: Whoever walks blamelessly is kept safe; but one with perverse ways will fall suddenly.

text.KJV: He that tilleth his land shall have plenty of bread: but he that followeth after vain persons shall have poverty enough.
text.ASV: He that tilleth his land shall have plenty of bread; But he that followeth after vain `persons' shall have poverty enough.
text.WEB: One who works his land will have an abundance of food; but one who chases fantasies will have his fill of poverty.

text.KJV: A faithful man shall abound with blessings: but he that maketh haste to be rich shall not be innocent.
text.ASV: A faithful man shall abound with blessings; But he that maketh haste to be rich shall not be unpunished.
text.WEB: A faithful man is rich with blessings; but one who is eager to be rich will not go unpunished.

text.KJV: To have respect of persons is not good: for for a piece of bread that man will transgress.
text.ASV: To have respect of persons is not good; Neither that a man should transgress for a piece of bread.
text.WEB: To show partiality is not good; yet a man will do wrong for a piece of bread.

text.KJV: He that hasteth to be rich hath an evil eye, and considereth not that poverty shall come upon him.
text.ASV: he that hath an evil eye hasteth after riches, And knoweth not that want shall come upon him.
text.WEB: A stingy man hurries after riches, and doesn’t know that poverty waits for him.

text.KJV: He that rebuketh a man afterwards shall find more favour than he that flattereth with the tongue.
text.ASV: He that rebuketh a man shall afterward find more favor Than he that flattereth with the tongue.
text.WEB: One who rebukes a man will afterward find more favor than one who flatters with the tongue.

text.KJV: Whoso robbeth his father or his mother, and saith, It is no transgression; the same is the companion of a destroyer.
text.ASV: Whoso robbeth his father or his mother, and saith, It is no transgression, The same is the companion of a destroyer.
text.WEB: Whoever robs his father or his mother, and says, “It’s not wrong.” He is a partner with a destroyer.

text.KJV: He that is of a proud heart stirreth up strife: but he that putteth his trust in the LORD shall be made fat.
text.ASV: He that is of a greedy spirit stirreth up strife; But he that putteth his trust in Jehovah shall be made fat.
text.WEB: One who is greedy stirs up strife; but one who trusts in Yahweh will prosper.

text.KJV: He that trusteth in his own heart is a fool: but whoso walketh wisely, he shall be delivered.
text.ASV: He that trusteth in his own heart is a fool; But whoso walketh wisely, he shall be delivered.
text.WEB: One who trusts in himself is a fool; but one who walks in wisdom is kept safe.

text.KJV: He that giveth unto the poor shall not lack: but he that hideth his eyes shall have many a curse.
text.ASV: He that giveth unto the poor shall not lack; But he that hideth his eyes shall have many a curse.
text.WEB: One who gives to the poor has no lack; but one who closes his eyes will have many curses.

text.KJV: When the wicked rise, men hide themselves: but when they perish, the righteous increase.
text.ASV: When the wicked rise, men hide themselves; But when they perish, the righteous increase.
text.WEB: When the wicked rise, men hide themselves; but when they perish, the righteous thrive.

text.KJV: He, that being often reproved hardeneth his neck, shall suddenly be destroyed, and that without remedy.
text.ASV: He that being often reproved hardeneth his neck Shall suddenly be destroyed, and that without remedy.
text.WEB: He who is often rebuked and stiffens his neck will be destroyed suddenly, with no remedy.

text.KJV: When the righteous are in authority, the people rejoice: but when the wicked beareth rule, the people mourn.
text.ASV: When the righteous are increased, the people rejoice; But when a wicked man beareth rule, the people sigh.
